newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan president sacks Bhutto, dissolves assembly.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan president sacks Bhutto, dissolves assembly.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Ahmed Leghari on Tuesday sacked Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and her cabinet and dissolved parliament, the official news agency APP said.
The agency said Bhutto and her cabinet would cease to hold office forthwith and quoted the president as announcing new elections in 90 days time.
The British Broadcasting Corporation's local correspondent said February 3 had been fixed as the date for a fresh election and said a caretaker prime minister had been appointed.
There was no immediate word on the whereabouts of the charismatic Bhutto, 43. But the BBC correspondent said she was in the prime minister's official residence in Islamabad.
"There are troops outside the house," he said, adding that she was "not officially under detention".
The BBC said the army was reported to have sealed all the country's airports. Troops were also outside television and radio stations.
Other witnesses said some army trucks were moving in the streets of Islamabad. Mobile telephone services had been disconnected.

"President Farooq Ahmed Leghari has dissolved National Assembly with immediate effect and the Prime Minister and her Cabinet will cease to hold office forthwith, it was announced today," the news agency said.

"I am satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the Government of the Federation cannot be carried on in accordancee with the provisions of the Constitution and an appeal to the electorate is necessary," it quoted a proclamation by the president as saying.
The BBC local correspondent said it did not feel as if a military coup was taking place -- more like a "kind of a constitutional coup".

Bhutto, charismatic daughter of Pakistan's first popularly elected leader, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, clawed her way back to recapture the position of prime minister of the Moslem state in October 1993 after three years in the political wilderness.
A mother of three, she inherited the leadership of the Pakistan's People's Party (PPP) after her father's controversial execution in 1979.
